items.title: Section: The Second Outward Means Opens — Teaching the Eight Precepts Correctly, the Middle Way Against Useless Austerity, and Genuine Meditation Against Reckless Extremes

items.zh: 云何菩薩方便善巧，令諸有情以少功力，引攝廣大無量善根？謂諸菩薩方便善巧，若有信解受邪齋戒，乃至一月都不食等諸有情類，為說八支聖齋戒法，令其棄捨最極艱辛感非愛果受邪齋戒，勸令修學無極艱辛感大愛果受正齋戒。若諸有情修自苦行，精勤無懈，起邪方便欲求解脫，為說中道，令離二邊，使其趣入。若諸有情求欲生天，起邪方便，投巖、赴火、斷飲食等，為其宣說無倒靜慮，令彼獲於現法樂住，逮得當來無諸艱苦、與喜樂俱生天勝果。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's skilful means enabling beings, expending only minimal effort, to gather vast, boundless wholesome roots? Bodhisattvas skilfully teach the eightfold noble fast to beings who, out of misguided faith, have adopted some wrong fasting vow, even going without food for an entire month, so that they abandon a wrong fast that is extremely arduous and yields an unwanted result, and instead undertake a correct fast that is not extremely arduous and yields a greatly desired result. Towards beings who diligently and unremittingly practice self-mortification, pursuing liberation through mistaken means, bodhisattvas teach the middle way, so that, freed of both extremes, they may enter the noble path. Towards beings who, wishing for celestial rebirth, pursue mistaken means such as leaping from cliffs, throwing themselves into fire, or abstaining from food, bodhisattvas proclaim undistorted meditative absorption, so that they may obtain present ease in this very life and, in the future, the supreme fruit of celestial rebirth joined with joy and bliss, free of all such hardship.

items.title: Section: Freeing Beings From Empty Ritual Into the Buddha's Own Teaching, and the Single Instant of Deep Faith That Outweighs Countless Ordinary Lifetimes

items.zh: 若諸有情信婆羅門吠地迦呪，妄計精勤受持、讀誦得究竟淨，方便勸令於佛聖教受持、讀誦、思惟其義。又正為他如是如是宣揚開示如來所說甚深空性相應妙法，令彼發生勇決厭離猛利淨信。但由如是一剎那頃厭離淨信俱行善心，尚能攝受不可稱數廣大善根，況其相續。又諸菩薩，世間所有種種上妙珍寶、香鬘、諸供養具，起淨信俱增上意樂，於佛法僧勝解供養，亦勸導他令行如是勝解供養。又於十方一切世界，一切供養佛法僧所，即以如是淨信俱行增上意樂，周匝普緣，深生隨喜，亦勸導他作是隨喜。
items.en: Towards beings who trust in the Brahmins' Vedic mantras, mistakenly supposing that diligently receiving and reciting them alone produces final purity, bodhisattvas skilfully guide them instead to receive, recite, and reflect on the meaning of the Buddha's own noble teaching. Bodhisattvas also, again and again, proclaim and reveal to others the Tathāgata's own profound teaching joined with emptiness, so that they give rise to a courageous, resolute, deeply renunciate, and forcefully pure faith. Simply through a single instant of wholesome mind joined with this renunciate, pure faith, one is already able to gather in an incalculable, vast wholesome root — how much more so, then, through its sustained continuity. Bodhisattvas also, towards every kind of supreme, wondrous jewel, fragrant garland, and offering implement found in the world, give rise to a heightened aspiration joined with pure faith, making offerings to the Buddha, the teaching, and the community through resolute visualisation, and also guide others to make these same visualised offerings. Furthermore, towards every occasion of offering to the Buddha, the teaching, and the community across every world of the ten directions, bodhisattvas, with this same heightened aspiration joined with pure faith, universally extend their attention all around and give rise to deep rejoicing, also guiding others to rejoice in this same way.

items.title: Section: The Six Recollections, Mental Prostration That Never Wastes a Moment, and Universal Rejoicing in Every Being's Own Merit

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，恒常修習念佛、念法，乃至念天，亦勸導他令修六念。又諸菩薩，意言分別禮佛法僧，乃至命終時無虛度，亦勸導他行此禮業。又諸菩薩，普於十方一切有情一切福業悉皆隨喜，亦勸導他作是隨喜。
items.en: Bodhisattvas also constantly cultivate recollection of the Buddha, of the teaching, and so on up through recollection of the celestial realms, and also guide others to cultivate these six recollections. Bodhisattvas also venerate the Buddha, the teaching, and the community through inner mental discourse and reflection, right up until the moment of death never once wasting this time, and also guide others to perform this same veneration. Bodhisattvas also universally rejoice in every wholesome deed of every being throughout the ten directions, and also guide others to rejoice in this same way.

items.title: Section: Vicarious Compassion, Confession That Dissolves Karmic Obstruction With Minimal Effort, Miraculous Generosity, and the Four Immeasurables Close the Fourteen Methods

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，普於十方一切有情，入廣大悲增上意樂，願以自身皆代彼受一切憂苦，亦勸導他興此悲願。又諸菩薩，過去現在一切誤失、一切違犯，以淨調柔愛樂隨順所學戒心，想對十方佛世尊所，至誠發露，悔往修來，亦勸導他令行是事。如是數數發露所犯，少用功力，一切業障皆得解脫。又諸菩薩，已具神通得心自在，普於十方佛法僧所及有情處，化作眾多種種化事，攝受無量大福德聚。又諸菩薩，恒常修習慈、悲、喜、捨，亦勸導他作此修習。如是菩薩以少功力，引攝廣大無量善根諸勝妙果。
items.en: Bodhisattvas also, universally towards all beings of the ten directions, enter a heightened aspiration joined with vast compassion, wishing with their own body to bear all their grief and suffering in their place, and also encourage others to raise this same compassionate vow. Bodhisattvas also, with a mind pure and pliant, delighting in and according with the precepts they have undertaken, visualising themselves before the buddhas and world-honoured ones of the ten directions, sincerely disclose every past and present error and violation, repenting what has passed and cultivating what is to come, and also guide others to do this same thing. Through disclosing what has been violated again and again in this way, using only minimal effort, one becomes entirely freed from every karmic obstruction. Bodhisattvas also, having already accomplished supernormal powers and attained mastery of mind, universally manifest, in the presence of the Buddha, the teaching, and the community throughout the ten directions, and in the presence of beings, many kinds of miraculous undertakings, thereby gathering in immeasurable, great accumulations of merit. Bodhisattvas also constantly cultivate loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity, and also guide others to cultivate these same states. In this way, bodhisattvas, expending only minimal effort, gather in vast, boundless wholesome roots and their many excellent fruits.

items.title: Section: Four Kinds of Being, Six Skilful Means to Reach Them — Accommodation Opens With Removing Hostility Before Ever Attempting to Teach

items.zh: 云何菩薩方便善巧，於佛聖教憎背有情，除其恚惱；處中住者，令其趣入；已趣入者，令其成熟；已成熟者，令得解脫？謂諸菩薩，為欲成辦如是四種有情義利，當知略說復有六種方便善巧。一者、隨順會通方便善巧，二者、共立要契方便善巧，三者、異分意樂方便善巧，四者、逼迫所生方便善巧，五者、施恩報恩方便善巧，六者、究竟清淨方便善巧。云何菩薩隨順會通方便善巧？謂諸菩薩，於彼有情將為說法，先當方便隨順現行軟美身語，亦復現行近施隨轉，除彼於己所生恚惱；彼恚惱除，便生愛敬。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's skilful means for removing hostility from beings who resent the Buddha's noble teaching; drawing those who remain neutral into genuine entry; maturing those who have already entered; and liberating those already mature? One should understand that bodhisattvas, wishing to accomplish the genuine benefit of these four kinds of being, have, in brief, six further kinds of skilful means: first, the skilful means of accommodation and reconciliation; second, the skilful means of mutual agreement; third, the skilful means of differing aspiration; fourth, the skilful means born of duress; fifth, the skilful means of kindness and its repayment; sixth, the skilful means of ultimate purity. Bodhisattvas, when about to teach such a being, first skilfully accommodate them by displaying gentle, agreeable speech and manner, and further display genuine closeness and material giving in accordance with that being's own inclination, thereby removing whatever hostility has arisen towards the bodhisattva; once that hostility is removed, affection and respect arise in its place.

blocks.text: Today continues the second outward skilful means: many small methods by which a bodhisattva turns beings' good intentions in a better direction. Then a new list of six opens.

They teach the eight precepts, so that beings give up an extremely arduous wrong fast that yields unwanted results. Master Cháng Bǎi: "pass" (關) means prohibition, closing the gate of beings' wandering in saṃsāra; "fast" (齋) means not eating after noon.
Venerable Miào Jìng: an offering is not just setting things down and being done; one must also visualise it in the mind.
"Recollection of the Buddha, the dharma, and so on up through recollection of the gods." Master Cháng Bǎi: venerating through mental words is the practice of bodhisattvas before the grounds.

"Disclosing violations again and again in this way, with little effort, one is freed from every karmic obstruction." Master Cháng Bǎi: visualise yourself before the buddhas of the ten directions, sincerely disclose and repent past wrongs. Venerable Miào Jìng: afflictions are rigid; when they are not active, the mind becomes gentle. (He notes that the English "gentle affection" reads this a little differently.)

First, accommodation and reconciliation; … sixth, ultimate purity. Venerable Miào Jìng: "maturing" is like apples or oranges ripening. Beings like to be agreed with, not opposed; the bodhisattva seeks nothing from them, only their benefit.

Confession here is not a ritual of self-blame. It is repeated, sincere disclosure that softens the mind, and the treatise says it takes "little effort". It is one of the most practical passages in the chapter.

quiz.q: For beings keeping wrong fasts, even a month without food, how does the bodhisattva guide them?
options: teach the eightfold noble fast — abandoning the arduous wrong fast with unwanted results for an easier one with desired results
quiz.why: They teach the eightfold noble fast, so that beings abandon an extremely arduous wrong fast yielding unwanted results and take up a correct fast, not arduous, yielding desired results. Master Cháng Bǎi: "fast" means not eating after noon.

quiz.q: How do the lectures explain the "eightfold noble fast"?
options: Cháng Bǎi: "pass" (關) means closing the gate of saṃsāra, "fast" means no food after noon; Miào Jìng: also called the near-dwelling discipline — dwelling near the arhats
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "pass" means prohibition — closing the gate of beings' wandering in saṃsāra; "fast" means not eating after noon. Venerable Miào Jìng: it is also called the near-dwelling discipline — dwelling near the arhats.

quiz.q: The six recollections run from what to what?
options: the Buddha, the dharma, up to the gods
quiz.why: "Recollection of the Buddha, the dharma, and so on up through recollection of the gods." Venerable Miào Jìng: "recollection" means visualising the Buddha; if you can't visualise, recite the name.

quiz.q: Through repeated confession with little effort, what is gained?
quiz.why: "Disclosing violations again and again in this way, with little effort, one is freed from every karmic obstruction." Master Cháng Bǎi: frequent confession keeps one from accumulating defilements.

quiz.q: Of the six means for the four kinds of beings, what are the first and the last?
quiz.why: First, accommodation and reconciliation; … sixth, ultimate purity. Venerable Miào Jìng: "maturing" is like apples or oranges in an orchard becoming ripe enough to eat.
